He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. As a sophomore in 2016–17, he earned second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] and was named the most outstanding player in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. ==High school career== [[File:20150401 MCDAAG Allonzo Trier putback.JPG|thumb|Trier at the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Trier attended [[Montrose Christian School]] in his junior year, transferring from the Oklahoma City Storm and Tulsa NOAH (Northeast Oklahoma Association of Homeschools). He averaged 25.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.8 assists. and 2.1 steals per game to lead Montrose to a 20–5 record and a National Christian Schools Athletic Association Division I title. He was named the 2014 Gatorade State Player of the Year and was a first-team Washington Post All-Met, elevating his recruiting stock.{{cite news|last1=Stubbs|first1=Roman|title=Allonzo Trier is a complicated case study of free agency in elite high school basketball|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/allonzo-trier-is-a-complicated-case-study-of-free-agency-in-elite-high-school-basketball/2014/08/08/37a43478-1bd0-11e4-ab7b-696c295ddfd1_story.html|access-date=October 13, 2016|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=August 8, 2014}} As a senior, Trier transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]]. He averaged 26.6 points and 5.4 rebounds per game at Findlay. He was named to the 2015 USA Today All-USA second team.{{cite web|title=Allonzo Trier|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/trier-allonzo.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623014013/http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/t/trier-allonzo.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 23, 2015|website=USA Basketball|access-date=October 13, 2016}} Playing for the West team in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], Trier led his team in scoring with 17 points.{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/04/01/cheick-diallo-leads-east-to-mcdonalds-all-american-game-victory/|title=Cheick Diallo leads East to McDonald's All-American Game victory|access-date=April 2, 2015|date=April 1, 2015|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} In the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], Trier scored 28 points and was named co-MVP. Trier committed to play at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] during an official visit due to his good relationship with coach [[Sean Miller]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=|year=2015}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Allonzo Trier | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Seattle, WA]] | highschool = [[The Henderson International School|Findlay Prep]] | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 190 | 40 = | commitdate = August 3, 2014 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = | rivals ref title = | espn ref title = | 247 ref title = | rivals school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = | 247 school = | accessdate = | bball = yes }} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== In an 85–72 victory over [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]] on December 10, 2015, Trier scored a season-high 27 points on 8-of-11 shooting.{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400813822|title=No. 13 Arizona pulls away for 85-72 win over Fresno State|access-date=October 13, 2016|work=[[ESPN]]|date=December 10, 2015}} He averaged 14.8 points per game in his freshman season but missed seven games due to a hand injury. On April 4, 2016, he announced he would be returning for his sophomore season.{{cite news|last1=Goodman|first1=Jeff|title=Allonzo Trier staying at Arizona|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15133640/allonzo-trier-forgoes-nba-draft-returns-arizona-wildcats|access-date=October 13, 2016|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 4, 2016}} ===Sophomore season=== Trier was suspended indefinitely for testing positive for [[Performance-enhancing substance|PED]]s; Trier was involved in a car crash and was given a drug. After the NCAA went over the medical documents, Trier was allowed to return.{{cite web|last1=Pascoe|first1=Bruce|title=Arizona Wildcats basketball: Allonzo Trier, Chance Comanche out for tonight's exhibition game|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-basketball-allonzo-trier-chance-comanche-out-for-tonight/article_343b466a-a0a2-11e6-ab14-cb89f282388c.html|website=Tucson.com|publisher=Arizona Daily Star|access-date=November 1, 2016}} On January 20, 2017, it was announced Trier would make his return for the UCLA game after 19 game absence.{{cite web|last1=Pascoe|first1=Bruce|title=Update: Suspended Wildcats guard Allonzo Trier to play Saturday vs. UCLA|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/update-suspended-wildcats-guard-allonzo-trier-to-play-saturday-vs/article_34e48f8c-df94-11e6-b168-371dff5072d4.html|website=Tucson.com|publisher=Arizona Daily Star|access-date=January 21, 2017}} As a sophomore in 2016–17, he earned second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] and was named the most outstanding player in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]]. ===Junior season=== On February 22, 2018, he was ruled ineligible by the NCAA after testing positive for a banned substance. According to Arizona, it was a remnant of the same substance he was banned for a year earlier.{{cite news|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|title=Arizona to appeal NCAA ruling after Allonzo Trier tests positive for banned substance|date=February 23, 2018|website=ESPN.com|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22547934/allonzo-trier-arizona-wildcats-ruled-ineligible}} Following Arizona's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]], Trier announced his intention to forgo his last season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/deandre-ayton-allonzo-trier-declare-nba-draft-arizonas-stunning-loss-045332084.html|title=Deandre Ayton, Allonzo Trier declare for NBA draft after Arizona's stunning loss|access-date=March 16, 2018|language=en-US}} ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2018–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], on July 3, 2018, Trier signed with the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the Knicks' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Westchester Knicks]]. Under the terms of that deal, Trier would split time between New York and Westchester.{{cite web| title = Knicks sign Isaiah Hicks and Allonzo Trier to two-way contracts | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = July 24, 2017 | url = https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-isaiah-hicks-and-allonzo-trier-two-way-contracts | access-date = July 3, 2018 }} In his NBA debut on October 17, Trier recorded 15 points on 5-of-9 shooting, four rebounds, and two blocks in a 126–107 win over the [[2018–19 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |last1=Astramskas |first1=David |title=Undrafted Knicks Rookie Allonzo Trier Shines In NBA Debut |url=http://ballislife.com/undrafted-knicks-rookie-allonzo-trier-shines-in-nba-debut/ |website=Ballislife.com |access-date=December 13, 2018 |date=October 18, 2018}} On November 23, Trier scored a career high 25 points in a 114–109 win over the [[2018–19 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |title=Knicks beat Pelicans, win consecutive games for first time |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070950 |website=ESPN |access-date=November 24, 2018 |date=November 23, 2018}} On November 27, he recorded his first career double-double with 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Knicks lost to the [[2018–19 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |title=New York Knicks win streak comes to an end against Detroit |url=https://eu.northjersey.com/story/sports/nba/knicks/2018/11/27/new-york-knicks-win-streak-ends-detroit-pistons/2132879002/ |website=North Jersey |access-date=March 7, 2019 |date=November 27, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Knicks' Allonzo Trier: Nears triple-double in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-allonzo-trier-nears-triple-double-in-loss/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=March 7, 2019 |date=November 27, 2018}} On December 13, Trier signed a standard NBA contract with the Knicks, becoming the first two-way player to sign a guaranteed NBA contract within the first two months of the season.{{cite web |title=New York Knicks Sign Allonzo Trier |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-sign-allonzo-trier |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 13, 2018 |date=December 13, 2018}} On January 23, 2019, Trier recorded his second career double-double, scoring a new career-high 31 points, shooting 12-for-18 from the field, and grabbing 10 rebounds in a 114–110 loss to the [[2018–19 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |title=Knicks' Allonzo Trier: Career-best performance in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-allonzo-trier-career-best-performance-in-loss/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=March 7, 2019 |date=January 23, 2019}} Trier made 64 appearances (including three starts) for New York during his rookie campaign, averaging 10.9 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 1.9 assists.{{Cite web|title=Allonzo Trier 2018-19 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3907525/type/nba/year/2019|access-date=April 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 14, 2019, the Knicks picked up the option on Trier's contract.{{cite web |last1=Begley |first1=Ian |title=Knicks pick up $3.5 million option for Allonzo Trier |url=https://www.sny.tv/knicks/news/knicks-pick-up-35-million-option-for-allonzo-trier/308096610 |website=SNY |access-date=September 18, 2019 |date=July 14, 2019}} On June 26, 2020, Trier was waived by the Knicks.{{cite web |title= New York Knicks Claim Theo Pinson Off Waivers|url= https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-claim-theo-pinson-off-waivers|website=NBA.com |access-date=June 26, 2020 |date= June 26, 2020}} ===Iowa Wolves (2021)=== On January 11, 2021, the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]] selected Trier with the fourth overall pick in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|January 2021 NBA G League draft]]{{cite web |title=NBA G League 2020-21 Draft Results |url=https://gleague.nba.com/nba-g-league-2020-21-draft-order/ |website=NBA G League |access-date=January 13, 2021 |date=January 8, 2021}} and he was later included in the team's roster.{{cite web |last1=Burrell |first1=Randi |title=Wolves Announce 2021 Roster |url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-2021-roster/ |website=iowa.gleague.nba.com |access-date=February 4, 2021 |date=January 25, 2021}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2024)=== On October 27, 2024, Trier signed with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite web|title=Vipers Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster/n-6160244|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} but was waived on November 7.{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Rio Grande Valley Vipers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Rio-Grande-Valley-Vipers/14/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 11, 2024}} ==National team career== He played in the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]] in 2014, winning a gold medal for the United States. He scored 9 points in the championship game.{{cite web|title=Boxscore - Team Leaders|url=http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/box.asp?g=20&n=A&r=10320&t=FOBKLVIJMF|website=[[FIBA]]|access-date=October 13, 2016|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304071527/http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/box.asp?g=20&n=A&r=10320&t=FOBKLVIJMF|url-status=dead}} In five games he averaged 12.6 points and 1.0 rebounds per game. Trier competed in the [[FIBA Under-19 World Championship|FIBA U19 World Championship]] in 2015, winning a gold medal for the United States. Trier posted averages of 8.7 points and 1.5 rebounds per game. ==Personal life== Trier was born in [[Seattle, Washington]], to Marcie Trier and a father whom he never met. When he was in sixth grade, he was diagnosed with dyslexia. He was kicked off a varsity team in eighth grade for being too good. In 2009, Trier was the subject of [[The New York Times Magazine]] profile of his ability at a young age and the frequent travelling for AAU events it entailed.{{cite news|last1=Sokolove|first1=Michael|title=Allonzo Trier Is in the Game|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/22/magazine/22basketball-t.html|access-date=October 13, 2016|work=[[The New York Times
